methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: WorkAI Lab at Roanoke College represents peer-based workforce training infrastructure outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for distributed AI capability building in underserved regions if the model scales beyond single institutions.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional backbone for broad community AI education, suggesting Richmond could emerge as a secondary distribution node that bridges the NoVA-rest-of-state gap through deliberate capability building.

signals.title: How Fairfax County police are using AI — and why opponents are concerned - NBC4 Washington
signals.signal_reading: Fairfax County police deploying AI surveillance tools demonstrates how deep technical implementation concentrates in well-resourced metro jurisdictions with capacity for complex adoption, while rural law enforcement lacks equivalent infrastructure.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Workforce pressure from AI adoption in Richmond signals platform-driven automation creating shallow, reactive engagement rather than proactive capability development—workers adapting to tools rather than shaping them.

signals.title: How AI is changing what happens to Hampton Roads' trash - The Suffolk News-Herald
signals.signal_reading: AI deployment in Hampton Roads waste management shows deep technical implementation in specific operational domains within metro areas, but sector-specific adoption doesn't necessarily translate to broader regional AI fluency or workforce capability.
